$comment: Lumos master constants register. Normative sources: TRS v1.1 Sec. 23 and EDP v1.0 Sec. 4 (ADR-004). This file is the single source of truth; LumosConstants.java, LumosConstants.swift and constants.go are generated from it by tools/constantsgen and are the ONLY permitted consumer surface (TRS-CONST-001). A hand-written constant in any language is a defect. Signed configuration may override only entries with overridable=true, and only within [min,max] (TRS-CONST-002). Changing any entry invalidates every golden vector that embeds constants_hash and therefore requires an approved change request plus vector regeneration (TRS-CONST-003).
baseline: TRS v1.1 Sec. 23 / EDP v1.0 Sec. 4 (ADR-004)
$service_uuid_provenance: One fixed 128-bit GATT service UUID per ADR-002 / TRS Sec. 9.3, generated once from a CSPRNG as an RFC 4122 version-4 UUID in WP-01 slice S2 and frozen here. Advertised by both platforms and used for scan filtering. No 16-bit alias is registered for flagship. Regenerating this value is a breaking protocol change.

constants_hash_algorithm.canonical_form: Every hashable leaf is flattened to a dotted path. Lines are '<path>=<value>', sorted bytewise by path as UTF-8, joined with '\n', with a single trailing '\n'.
constants_hash_algorithm.value_rendering: integer -> decimal with '-' for negatives; boolean -> 'true'/'false'; string -> verbatim UTF-8; array of scalars -> '[' + elements joined by ',' + ']'; array of objects -> recursed by zero-based index as a path segment. There are deliberately NO floating-point values in this register, so no float formatting rule is required and none may be introduced.
constants_hash_algorithm.excluded_keys: Any key beginning with '$', plus the fixed set: constants_hash, constants_hash_algorithm, anchors, source, notes, adr.
constants_hash_algorithm.rationale: A flattened key=value form is chosen over canonical JSON because it is trivially reimplementable in Java, Swift and Go without depending on any library's key-ordering or number-formatting behaviour. Documentation-only fields are excluded so that editing a requirement reference or a comment does not invalidate the golden vectors; every value-bearing field is included.

ADV_AUTH_TAG_LEN.notes: Bytes. First 4 bytes of HMAC-SHA-256(K_adv, version|modeFlags|rotatingEid|epoch); Android pre-connection noise rejection only.

ADV_V1_LAYOUT.notes: TRS 9.3 adv_v1 = version(1) | modeFlags(1) | rotatingEid(12) | authTag(4). Android Service Data hint only; iOS advertises the service UUID alone and never service data (ADR-002). Content is an unauthenticated routing hint - canonical trust is re-established in HELLO/HELLO_ACK (TRS-PROTO-017).

ADV_V1_SCAN_RESPONSE_LAYOUT.notes: TRS 9.3 Android scan response = capabilityBits(2) | venueHint(4).

RSSI_BANDS_DBM.notes: Three bands are fully determined by two thresholds: very close >= -55; nearby in [-75,-55); around venue < -75.

NEARBY_SYNTHETIC_LOAD_TARGET.notes: Synthetic peer count the discovery view must remain responsive under. Present in EDP 4.1 only; TRS 23.1 omits it. Added in WP-01 slice S2 with owner approval.

SAFETY_NUMBER_FORMAT.notes: 60 decimal digits plus 6 emoji TOTAL (not 6 pairs), drawn from a fixed curated 64-emoji alphabet. The alphabet itself is frozen by WP-01 slice S4 in test-vectors/crypto/safety_number.json. Resolves the TRS 23.2 '6-emoji pair' ambiguity per ADR-005 (Accepted).

CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SEC.notes: Plus or minus, with server hint.

BLE_CHUNK_PAYLOAD.notes: Derived at runtime from the negotiated ATT MTU.

FRAG_HEADER_LEN.notes: Transport fragment header, fixed here per the TRS Sec. 19 AI delivery rule (layout unstated by the TRS, frozen once vectors exist - WP-03 S2). Byte 0 flags, byte 1 assembly_id (u8, per-link, wraps), bytes 2-3 fragment_index (u16 big-endian, 0-based, strictly sequential). This is where BLE_CHUNK_PAYLOAD's subtract-7 comes from: 3 bytes ATT write overhead + these 4. The layer is content-opaque (TRS-PROTO-010): it carries bytes, never a parsed frame.

FRAG_FLAG_FIRST.notes: Header byte 0, bit 0. The first fragment of an assembly; its content begins with the u32 big-endian total length of the reassembled blob (FRAG_TOTAL_PREFIX_LEN).

FRAG_FLAG_LAST.notes: Header byte 0, bit 1. FIRST|LAST together is a single-fragment message.

FRAG_FLAGS_RESERVED_MASK.notes: 0xFC - header byte 0 bits 2..7. Any set reserved bit fails closed with ERR_FRAG_HEADER_MALFORMED: the fragment layer has no critical-flag escape hatch because nothing semantic rides in it.

FRAG_TOTAL_PREFIX_LEN.notes: u32 big-endian reassembled-length prefix carried in the FIRST fragment's content, so bounds are validated before any reassembly allocation (TRS Sec. 9.4, TRS-PROTO-007 discipline applied at this layer).

FRAG_REASSEMBLY_MAX_BYTES.notes: FRAME_HEADER_LEN_BYTES (58) + the largest per-class payload bound (media.FULL_IMAGE_MAX_MB, 2097152): no legal semantic frame can exceed this, so a FIRST fragment declaring more is rejected before allocation. A Go test holds this value to that derivation so it cannot silently fall behind a raised class bound.

FRAG_MAX_FRAGMENTS.notes: fragment_index is u16, 0-based, so one assembly holds at most 65536 fragments. The sender fails a split that would need more (a 2 MB PROFILE_FULL does not fit over a floor-20 degraded link); the transfer is refused at the sender rather than stalling the receiver.

VOICE_NOTE.notes: VOICE_NOTE_PROFILE (codec, sample rate, bitrate, max_kb) is FIXED per TRS 23.5; only VOICE_NOTE_MAX duration is overridable, within 30..180 s. overridable_fields narrows the entry-level flag to that one field so the generated config schema cannot offer the fixed profile as a signed-config target.

resource_budgets.$section_notes: TRS 23.7. Release-gated budgets, regression-tracked per TRS-CICD-010. None are overridable by signed configuration. Absent from the handover seed; added in WP-01 slice S2 because TRS Sec. 23 is normative in full.

COLD_LAUNCH_P95_MS.notes: TRS 23.7 states 2.0 s. Encoded in milliseconds as an integer so the register contains no floating-point value and constants_hash needs no float-formatting rule.

IDLE_BACKGROUND.notes: TRS 23.7 states '~0%; no wake locks' for visibility-off idle. Encoded as a 0% ceiling plus an explicit prohibition on wake locks.

framing.$section_notes: TRS Sec. 9.1 canonical frame header. Field widths and order are normative; byte offsets follow from them in declaration order, network byte order (big-endian). Flag bit positions are NOT stated by TRS Sec. 9.1 - the TRS names the four flag meanings and leaves the encoding to the implementation (TRS Sec. 19 AI delivery rule). They are fixed here and become frozen wire format once WP-01 slice S4 generates vectors.

PROTOCOL_VERSION.notes: TRS 9.1 says 'current major/minor encoded per schema' without fixing the encoding. Chosen: one u8, high nibble major, low nibble minor, so v1.0 = 0x10. A frame whose major differs from PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAJOR fails closed (TRS-PROTO-006); a differing minor is accepted.

FRAME_HEADER_LEN_BYTES.notes: Sum of the thirteen TRS 9.1 fields. The complete immutable header is authenticated as AEAD associated data (TRS-PROTO-003), so this is exactly the AAD length for a v1 frame carrying no header extension.

FRAME_FLAG_CRITICAL.notes: Bit 0. Set means a receiver that does not understand this frame must fail closed rather than skip it (TRS-PROTO-006).

FRAME_FLAG_COMPRESSED.notes: Bit 1. Compression is optional and negotiated; decompression is bounded against decompression bombs (TRS-PROTO-008).

FRAME_FLAG_RELAY_ELIGIBLE.notes: Bit 2. Clear means no relay may forward the frame.

FRAME_FLAG_LOCAL_ONLY.notes: Bit 3. Set means the frame must never traverse the internet relay. Media and voice notes are local-only in flagship (SRS-TRN-009); this flag makes that checkable at the transport boundary rather than trusted by convention.

FRAME_FLAGS_RESERVED_MASK.notes: 0xFFF0 - bits 4..15. A frame setting any reserved bit while also setting FRAME_FLAG_CRITICAL fails closed; otherwise the unknown bits are ignored (TRS-PROTO-006).

crypto_protocol.$section_notes: Cryptographic domain-separation strings, transcript-binding constants and the safety-number alphabet (TRS-CRY-014, ADR-001, ADR-005). All frozen: none is overridable by signed configuration. These are protocol constants shared by all three platforms and therefore live in the register, not in source (TRS-CONST-001). The X3DH identity-DH key model is ADR-008 (provisional).

X3DH_KDF_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info string for the X3DH shared-secret derivation.

X3DH_TRANSCRIPT_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the transcript hash binding identity keys, identity-DH keys, signed-prekey ID, one-time-prekey ID, protocol version and match ID. The transcript hash is the associated data of the first ratchet message (TRS Sec. 10.1 first-message binding).

X3DH_IDENTITY_BINDING_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the Ed25519 signature binding a device identity-DH X25519 key to its Ed25519 identity (ADR-008).

X3DH_PREKEY_SIGNING_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the Ed25519 signature over (info | spk_id | spk_pub).

X3DH_F_PREFIX.notes: Per the X3DH spec, HKDF input is F || DH1..DHn where F is 32 bytes of 0xFF for Curve25519, providing cryptographic domain separation from the curve encoding.

X3DH_OPK_ID_NONE.notes: Sentinel one-time-prekey ID in the transcript when the responder had no one-time prekey available (documented fallback per TRS-CRY-005).

RATCHET_ROOT_KDF_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info string of KDF_RK(root_key, dh_output) -> (root_key, chain_key).

RATCHET_MESSAGE_KDF_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info string deriving (encryption key 32 | nonce 12) from a message key. Nonces never repeat under a key because every message key is used exactly once (TRS-CRY-011).

CHAIN_KEY_SEEDS.notes: KDF_CK per the Double Ratchet spec: message_key = HMAC-SHA-256(chain_key, 0x01), next chain_key = HMAC-SHA-256(chain_key, 0x02).

RATCHET_HEADER_LAYOUT.notes: Ratchet message header: dh_public(32) | pn(4,BE) | n(4,BE). Rides at the head of the frame payload; the AEAD associated data is frame_header(58) || ratchet_header(40), satisfying TRS-PROTO-003 and authenticated ratchet headers simultaneously.

HELLO_V1_LAYOUT.notes: The HELLO payload (class 0x01), fixed here per the TRS Sec. 19 AI delivery rule (WP-03 S4): protocol_version (encoded, re-confirmed in-band per TRS-PROTO-017) | hello_version (=1) | capabilityBits | venueHint | current rotating EID (zeros when no hint is advertised) | Ed25519 identity public | X25519 identity-DH public | ADR-008 binding signature | fresh nonce. Everything the advertisement hinted is re-established HERE, authenticated; the hint itself is never trusted.

HELLO_ACK_V1_LAYOUT.notes: HELLO_ACK (0x02) = the responder's own hello_v1 fields followed by auth_sig: Ed25519 over UTF-8(HELLO_AUTH_INFO) | SHA-256(the initiator's exact HELLO payload bytes) | every ACK byte before the signature. Freshness comes from the initiator's nonce inside that hash; presence is granted ONLY to a peer whose ACK answers one's own fresh HELLO, so both sides run the exchange once per link direction and a replayed message grants nothing (TRS-ENV-002).

HELLO_AUTH_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the HELLO_ACK authentication signature.

PEER_ID_KDF_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the public peer identifier: PEER_ID_LEN bytes of SHA-256(info | Ed25519 identity public). Derived from cryptographic identity material and nothing else - no MAC address, phone number or store account anywhere near it (SRS-IDN-002). Presence and dedup key on this identifier, which is stable across EID rotations (SRS-NBY-006).

PEER_ID_LEN.notes: Bytes of the derived peer identifier.

ADV_KEY_KDF_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info deriving K_adv from the peer's long-term advertisement secret. K_adv is per-identity and never leaves the device.

ADV_EID_KDF_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info deriving the rotating ephemeral identifier for an epoch: EID = HKDF(K_adv, info | epoch_be64)[0:eid_len]. Rotation cadence is identity_discovery.EID_ROTATION_SEC, so epoch = floor(unix_seconds / EID_ROTATION_SEC) and the payload is uncorrelatable across epochs (SRS-IDN-004).

ADV_AUTH_TAG_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the advertisement authTag: first ADV_AUTH_TAG_LEN bytes of HMAC-SHA-256(K_adv, info | version | mode_flags | rotating_eid | epoch_be64). Noise rejection only; it confers no trust (TRS-PROTO-017).

MEDIA_OBJECT_KEY_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info deriving the whole-object AEAD key and nonce from the random object key. The object is encrypted in full BEFORE fragmentation (TRS-CRY-008).

MEDIA_OBJECT_KEY_WRAP_INFO.notes: HKDF-SHA-256 info deriving the wrapping key that binds an object key to the active match session, so an object key is useless outside its session (TRS-CRY-008).

CONFIG_SIGNING_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the Ed25519 signature over a signed configuration package's canonical payload bytes (TRS-CRY-009).

VOUCHER_SIGNING_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of the Ed25519 signature over a voucher token's canonical payload bytes (TRS-CRY-009).

SAFETY_NUMBER_KDF_INFO.notes: Domain prefix of both the per-identity fingerprint iteration and the emoji-index derivation.

SAFETY_NUMBER_ITERATIONS.notes: Iterated-hash count per identity fingerprint, matching the Signal safety-number hardening factor.

SAFETY_NUMBER_EMOJI_ALPHABET.notes: The frozen 64-glyph alphabet of ADR-005, selected under the ADR-009 security criterion: single-codepoint default-emoji-presentation glyphs only (no ZWJ, no variation selectors, no skin-tone or gender variants), distinct silhouettes, no colour-only distinctions. Per-glyph rationale in docs/adrs/ADR-009-safety-number-emoji-alphabet.md. 64 glyphs = 6 bits each; 6 glyphs carry 36 bits.

RECOVERY_ARGON2ID.notes: Argon2id parameters for the ADR-003 content-only RecoveryRecord, added in WP-02 slice S4. NOT overridable by signed configuration: a config that lowered them would weaken every export made afterwards, and the whole point of a passphrase-derived key is that its cost is fixed by us rather than by whoever controls a config feed. 64 MiB / 3 passes / 1 lane is the OWASP-shaped balance for a mobile device that must also do this while the user waits. The memory and time bounds exist for a different reason from every other bounded entry here: a RecoveryRecord CARRIES its own parameters so that a record written today still opens after the defaults move, and import refuses any record whose parameters fall below these minima - which is what stops an attacker who can edit the file from downgrading the work factor before a passphrase guess. parallelism, salt_bytes and key_bytes are fixed and unbounded because changing any of them is a format change, not a tuning knob. parallelism carried min/max until CR-001 (WP-02 S4c) removed them: libsodium crypto_pwhash exposes no multi-lane Argon2 entry point and libsodium is the binding on both mobile platforms, so a lane count above 1 describes a record no shipping platform can open. That is a portability floor, deliberately the opposite shape of the memory and time ceilings above, and a range of legal values for it never existed.

onboarding_safety.$section_notes: Onboarding, consent and safety-action policy values. Added in WP-02 slice S4c. TRS Sec. 23 has no onboarding section because none of these values crosses a device boundary - but ADR-004 is about tunable values, not about wire values, and a hard-coded 18 in an age gate is exactly the magic number it exists to forbid.

ADULT_AGE_MINIMUM.notes: The global adult-only floor. SRS-NFR-LEG-007 states it plainly: the adult-only 18+ gate applies globally. NOT overridable by signed configuration, and the asymmetry is deliberate - SRS-NFR-LEG-007 also allows jurisdictions with stricter duties to be gated per-market via configuration, but 'stricter' is the only direction that is ever safe and this register has no way to express a one-directional bound. An overridable entry with a [min,max] range would let a compromised or misconfigured config feed LOWER the age gate on a dating product, which SRS Sec. 2.4's stricter-reading rule forbids. Per-market raising therefore belongs to the work package that owns market configuration, as a separate entry with its own floor at this value and an approved change request; until then this number is the gate on every market. The gate stores only the affirmation and the value it was checked against (privacy data map Sec. 2.3) - never the date of birth it was computed from.

VISIBLE_NEARBY_DURATION_SEC.notes: SRS-NBY-001's bounded visibility durations: default one hour, and [min,max] is BOTH the signed-config override range for the default AND the range a user's custom duration may take (fifteen minutes to eight hours). Until-venue-exit is a MODE, not a duration - it ends on the venue-exit event and still never renews itself (SRS-NBY-002). The eight-hour ceiling is a privacy bound: visibility that quietly spans a day stops being a session someone chose.

message_classes.$section_notes: TRS Sec. 9.2 canonical message classes. Generated into a typed enum in all three languages so no wire code hand-writes a class byte (TRS-CODE-005, TRS-PAT-006). Adding or changing a class is a protocol change under TRS-PROTO-016 and moves constants_hash by design.

classes.name: TEXT_MESSAGE
classes.purpose: Ratcheted private text event carrying the inner event envelope (AMD-005)

text_event_kinds.name: EDIT
text_event_kinds.purpose: Authenticated edit over the original message

text_event_kinds.name: DELETE_FOR_EVERYONE
text_event_kinds.purpose: Authenticated delete over the original message

text_event_kinds.name: REACTION
text_event_kinds.purpose: Authenticated reaction over the original message

message_classes.$text_event_notes: AMD-005 / TRS Sec. 9.2 class 0x10. Kinds 1..3 carry target_message_id. Unknown event_kind values follow TRS-PROTO-006 (safe skip if non-critical, fail closed if critical).
